social competence is an important factor in determining the directionality of the development of psychopathology.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the social competence of vulnerable children is a prime predictor of their long-term outcome and that this social competence is best measured by peer ratings.
the peer status and the direction of the symptomatic behavior are more important predictors of outcome than the nature of the child's risk.
